assert.rubric: The review names what to cut and its concrete replacement, one line per finding (e.g. flags the hand-rolled email regex class and points to a stdlib/standard alternative or a one-liner). It is NOT vague prose praise, hedged open-ended questions, or a wall of explanation. A passing answer reads as terse, surgical cut instructions and quantifies the line savings.

The review flags the moment.js dependency as unnecessary for a single date format and names the native replacement (e.g. toISOString().slice(0,10) or Intl/Date). It states the cut concisely, one line per finding, and quantifies the savings — NOT vague praise, NOT hedged questions, NOT a long essay.

The review flags the single-implementation abstraction (the ABC and/or the factory with one backend) as YAGNI and says to collapse it to the concrete class. Findings are concise, one line each, naming what to delete and what remains — NOT vague praise, NOT hedged 'have you considered' questions, NOT a wall of prose. The line savings are quantified.

The review flags the hand-rolled character-by-character loop as reducible and shows the shorter form (e.g. a single regex replace chain). It is a concise cut instruction, one line per finding, naming the replacement — NOT vague praise, NOT open-ended questions, NOT a long explanatory paragraph. The line savings are quantified.
